correctness.rationale: Full original three-variable ODE independently reconstructed. Both cost faces invariant; the critical first integral has directly verified gradient cancellation and strictly positive diagonal Hessian at its unique interior equilibrium. Local regular levels are periodic circles. Full-period logit identities give exact mean cooperation and weighted risk. Strict binomial modal gap proves positive risk surplus, and triangular linearization gives the claimed normal Floquet exponent. Four symbolic parameter checks and two integrated return maps passed. No finite test substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 paper already defines the same fixed-cost planar equations and studies oscillations. Neither that two-coordinate system nor its Hopf discussion yields a normal Floquet multiplier in the third, dynamically evolving cost coordinate. The 2026 article introduces that third equation and reports equilibrium stability tests using strict inequalities; the exact amplitude-dependent normal exponent, strict mean-risk surplus, and opposite-face example do not follow from its stated equilibrium classifications. The 2024 paper couples cooperation to dilemma strength with risk not coevolving in the same three-coordinate way. Searches were checked for implication-equivalent and stronger coverage, and older overlapping interior recurrence results have different support and conclusions.

value.rationale: At the precise resonance outside the motivating article’s strict stable-equilibrium regime, the result quantifies a finite-amplitude excess of collective risk on every cycle and proves that this excess shifts full-system cost-normal growth with an opposite sign on the two extreme-cost faces. One fully specified, biologically/socially natural parameter tuple realizes repulsion at minimum cost and attraction at maximum cost, revealing a nontrivial selection mechanism absent from the two-variable fixed-cost predecessor. No assertion of global basins or isolated stable cycles.
